Definition: from G3049; computation, i.e. (figuratively) reasoning (conscience, conceit):--imagination, thought.
BiblicalUsage: logismós means imagination, thought, and once is enough to see what it is doing. In Romans 2:15, "and [their] thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another"; and in 2 Corinthians 10:4, "but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe thoughts are strongholds — the weapons of our warfare pull them down, and the conscience bears witness whether they accuse or excuse.
